$comment: Gated thresholds for the Phase 16.3A risk evaluation.
Version-controlled on purpose: changing what 'good enough' means is a
reviewable decision, not a runtime flag. `gated: true` metrics decide the
CLI exit code; `gated: false` metrics are reported for observation only.
Bounds are deliberately modest. This is a capability lab on a minimum-
capacity deployment, not a model quality benchmark, and a threshold that
fails on ordinary variance teaches nothing.

schema_validity_rate.rationale: Structured output is the capability under test. Any schema failure is a real finding, so this is the one metric held at 100%.

classification_accuracy.rationale: Six-way classification over deliberately borderline cases; well above the 0.17 chance rate while tolerating genuine ambiguity.

escalation_accuracy.rationale: Binary decision balanced 6/6 in the dataset, so 0.5 is chance. 0.75 requires real signal.

evidence_validity_rate.rationale: Evidence ids are copied verbatim from the observation. Inventing one is fabrication, which matters more than a debatable severity.

repeated_call_consistency.rationale: Fraction of cases whose repetitions all agree. Sampling makes some disagreement expected; collapse below this means results are not reproducible enough to trust.

provider_error_rate.rationale: Transport and rate-limit failures are tolerable in small numbers on a capacity-1 deployment; a sustained rate means the endpoint, not the model, is the problem.

severity_accuracy.rationale: Observational only. Severity is the most subjective field in the schema and is not a fair gate for a lab.

latency_p95_ms.rationale: Observational only. Latency on a shared sandbox deployment says more about the service than about this code.
